Summary: evaluating Redwood Dedicated to replace current self-hosted serving for low-latency market data personalization. Primary focus is rigorous alignment on latency SLO definitions and how those are measured (client-side end-to-end vs server-side service time) before we sign a reserve.

Recent timeline:
- 2025-11-05: initial inbound, product team evaluation (created).
- 2025-11-20: discovery call (Jordan + Priya + infra lead). Covered high-level throughput needs.
- 2026-01-15: deep-dive workshop (Fireflies ff_02H9LQ_tidegate-slo-workshop). Recorded.
- 2026-02-02: Redwood delivered draft SLO matrix + sizing worksheet (Drive link).
- 2026-03-01: internal POC run of small sample model on GPU farm, measured server-side p95 ~170ms (non-streaming).
- 2026-03-09: SLO negotiation call; agreed to run 72h stress test on proposed Dedicated pool.

Use-case details / requirements (as told by TideGate infra/product):
- Workload: user-facing chat + high-frequency reranking for market signals. Typical request size small (200-800 tokens), but bursts during market open can spike 6x.
- Throughput target: steady 400 req/s, peak 2400 req/s burstable (30s windows). Need predictable tail latency under burst.
- Latency targets requested by product: p50 < 30ms (server compute), p95 < 150ms (end-to-end for non-streaming), p99 < 350ms (end-to-end). Streaming is allowed for chat; they expect different measurement rules there (first-token p95 < 120ms, full-stream completion p99 softer).
- Cost sensitivity: medium-high. Prefer Reserved capacity + autoscale bursts into hosted or spare Dedicated pools.
- Model preferences: using LLaMA-3 style family quantized to 4-bit where possible; fallback to fp16 for quality-critical reranking. Prefer transparent model variant routing and canarying.
- Security/compliance: must live in their VPC, keys in their KMS, audit logging retained for 13 months, SAML SSO for console access, SOC2 required.

Key SLO measurement alignment items (open/under discussion):
- Measurement source: TideGate insists on client-side (edge-agent) end-to-end measurements for p95/p99 because network and gateway time materially affect user experience. Redwood proposal includes both server-side service time and optional client-side synthetic probes. Need formal spec to avoid disagreement on credits.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: agreed that streaming should be decoupled; p50/p95 for first-token latency measured server-side, but full response completeness tail measured end-to-end with leniency. Documented example in draft SLO matrix.
- Percentile windows: prefer 1-minute sliding windows for p95 but monthly aggregated for SLA. Redwood suggests 5m windows to smooth variance; TideGate wants evidence from 72h stress to accept.
- Tail measurement methodology: use HdrHistogram + reservoir sampling for real traffic. Need clarity if p99 for SLA is computed on aggregated traffic or per-route. TideGate requires per-route (reranking route separate).

POC / sizing notes:
- Initial proposal: 16x A100-equivalent GPUs for baseline pool (predictable throughput ~600 req/s for their 8k token model), with autoscale gates to add 8 GPUs for burst windows.
- Engineering question: concurrency vs batching trade-offs for worst-case p99 under burst. Priya recommended testing small-batch, low-latency config (batch_size=1-4) and a separate high-batch throughput lane.

Commercial / SLA negotiation points:
- TideGate wants inclusion of p95 and p99 targets in SLO table with credits tied to client-measured end-to-end p95 failures. Redwood prefers server-side defaults and credits scoped to server time.
- Proposed compromise: dual-reporting (server-side primary for internal ops and client-side for credits) with an agreed mapping function. Need legal & finance to sign off.

Action items (next steps):
- Redwood to produce formal "Latency SLO Measurement Spec" that defines: exact events to timestamp (client send, server receive, server send, client receive), how to instrument SDK/edge agent, aggregation windows, and the mapping used to convert server metrics to client-facing credit calculations. Due: 2026-03-17 (Priya).
- TideGate to provide representative traffic replay dataset and peak-times schedule for 72h stress run. Due: 2026-03-12 (TideGate infra).
- Run 72h stress on proposed Dedicated pool (Jordan + Priya + TideGate infra) then sync to review p50/p95/p99 across streaming and non-streaming.
- Legal to align SLA credit language once measurement spec finalized.

Risks & open concerns:
- If client-side network variance dominates tail, dedicated GPUs won't move the needle; need telemetry to separate causes.
- Reranking quality fallback to fp16 increases compute cost; need cost vs accuracy tradeoff evaluated in POC.
- Legal pushback on credits tied to client-side metrics — needs mapping to avoid double-counting.
